storyboard.claim: Gray's rage is about ownership, not love — he feels robbed of an asset.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray, furious, pointing — the CEO-style outrage of a stolen asset, not a broken heart.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the CEO/corporate-asset framing of Gray's rage.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the specific emotion — narcissistic injury over ownership — instead of romantic jealousy.

storyboard.claim: Avery's realization is not a dramatic twist but a slow, sick dawning.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery standing still, processing — no gasp, no scene, just a slow interior shift.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up HOW Avery discovers the truth about Gray.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contradicts the genre's expected 'dramatic twist' — this realization is quiet and dragging.

storyboard.claim: Avery sees his bloodied knuckles and the hatred in his eyes and no longer recognizes him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery frozen, staring at Gray, who stands apart from her — the man she thought she knew is gone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The concrete moment the slow dawn (201) lands.
storyboard.addedInformation: Specifies exactly what she sees — bloodied knuckles, pure hatred — that breaks the illusion.

storyboard.claim: The illusion shatters completely — Avery is exposed to the actual monster she has been sleeping beside.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The crack — the illusion breaking apart — beside Avery reeling from what she now sees.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The moment of recognition (202) becomes total collapse of the illusion.
storyboard.addedInformation: Marks this as a full break, not a doubt — 'completely shatters,' 'actual monster.'

storyboard.claim: The performance is over, Avery is isolated, and her nervous system is bound to a predator.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray's true, unmasked face — no more charm to hide behind.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows directly from 203's shattered illusion — now stated outright.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the isolation is 'complete' and the entanglement may be 'permanent' — this is the point of no return.

storyboard.claim: Transition line into the episode's final topic: the book's ending.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery and Gray held in the same tense scene as the hosts pivot topics.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pure show transition, continuing the previous visual.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: no new information, a segment bridge.

storyboard.claim: Dark romance lives or dies on its ending — and this one offers no exit.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery reaching against chains — there is no way out of Lilyale.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the episode's final topic: does this story offer any escape?
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the ending as defined by what's missing — an exit — not what happens.

storyboard.claim: Poses the genre's two stock endings — healing the bad boy, or escaping together — before rejecting both.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery and Gray walking together — the fairy-tale escape the genre usually promises.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The rhetorical question the previous beat's 'no exit' sets up.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: stages the hypothetical the narration is about to reject, not what actually happens.

storyboard.claim: Macca refuses both stock endings — there is no clean, moralistic rescue.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery alone, unrescued — no one arrives to fix this.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Directly rejects the hypothetical staged in 207.
storyboard.addedInformation: The negation itself is the information — this beat exists to say what does NOT happen.

callout.text: TATTOOED A FIST ON HIS FACE

storyboard.claim: Violence at Lilyale escalates — Theo permanently tattoos a fist onto Sam's face as punishment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Theo holding the tattoo needle over Sam — the permanent fist design inked onto his face as a brutal, lasting punishment.
storyboard.onScreenText: TATTOOED A FIST ON HIS FACE
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The 'no rescue' promise of 208 becomes concrete: things get violently worse instead.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the specific, permanent act — not generic prison violence.

callout.text: NO AUTHORITY COMING TO SAVE THEM

storyboard.claim: The chaos is absolute and no one in authority is coming to intervene.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery alone amid the unraveling institution, no staff or guard present.
storyboard.onScreenText: NO AUTHORITY COMING TO SAVE THEM
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Widens 209's specific violence into the facility's total collapse of oversight.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes the absence of any outside intervention — sets up Avery's own resignation next.

storyboard.claim: Avery's internal monologue is not escape-planning but blunt acceptance of how far gone she already is.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery sitting alone, reciting her own condition to herself.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers 210's 'no one is coming' with Avery's own resigned self-assessment.
storyboard.addedInformation: Uses her literal words — this is her own voice, not the narrator's interpretation.

storyboard.claim: Avery concludes there's only one direction left for her — profound acceptance, not resistance.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery walking forward, resigned, toward the only path she believes remains.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes Avery's quoted thought from 211.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: restates her conclusion visually rather than adding new information.

storyboard.claim: Macca neither validates the Avery-Gray dynamic as healthy nor offers a fairy-tale rescue — Avery assimilates into the darkness.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery's shadow self — the darker version of her the story concludes she becomes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names what Avery's 'one direction' (212) actually is.
storyboard.addedInformation: Clarifies this is neither endorsement nor rescue — a third, bleaker outcome.

storyboard.claim: Dr. Smith offered Avery a clinical, transactional path toward health — but it felt alien to her.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dr. Smith, notes in hand, offering Avery his clinical treatment path.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the contrast between the treatment Avery was offered and the one she chose.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes Dr. Smith's option existed — the 'darkness' Avery chose wasn't the only path.

storyboard.claim: Avery weighed two offers: Dr. Smith's clinical help against Gray and Theo's toxic, all-consuming belonging.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The spectrum between clinical distance and enveloping toxic belonging.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns 214's single offer into the full choice Avery faced.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the two options and their imbalance visible at once, not sequential.

storyboard.claim: Avery's trauma-shaped biology chose the toxic belonging because it's the only frequency her wiring can tune into.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery and Gray in silhouette — her decision was biological, not a clear-eyed choice.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Resolves the spectrum in 215 — explains WHY she chose the toxic side.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the choice as neurological compulsion, not conscious preference.

callout.text: A BROKEN LOCK ON HER DOOR

storyboard.claim: It's a tragedy — Avery has lived her whole life with a fundamentally broken lock.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery alone, carrying the damage the metaphor describes.
storyboard.onScreenText: A BROKEN LOCK ON HER DOOR
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends 216's biological framing into the book's central lock-and-key metaphor.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the lock metaphor that the following beats build on.

storyboard.claim: The polite doctors couldn't fix her broken lock — but Gray, himself broken and jagged, fits it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray holding the key — the broken, jagged shape that matches Avery's broken lock.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces Gray as the literal key to the lock named in 217.
storyboard.addedInformation: Specifies Gray himself is damaged too — the fit is between two broken things, not a fix.

storyboard.claim: The key turns, the door opens — but only to let the monster in permanently.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The chain of cause and effect from the key turning to the monster's entry.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows what happens once Gray (the key, 218) fits Avery's lock.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the mechanism explicit as a sequence, not just a static image.

storyboard.claim: The damaged lock and key interlock flawlessly, sealing Avery inside the house.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery bound in chains — trapped inside, not freed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The flow in 219 completes: the door closes behind the monster with Avery still inside.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the outcome is permanent entrapment, the summary line before the show's recap begins.

storyboard.claim: Unhinged is more than a toxic romance — it's a meticulous manual for how trauma rewires a person.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The book itself — Macca's text as the literal manual the narration describes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the recap by restating the episode's whole thesis.
storyboard.addedInformation: Reframes everything shown so far as a demonstrated mechanism, not just a plot.

storyboard.claim: Turns the lens on the viewer: why study this dynamic at all?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Everyman figure, standing in for the viewer, considering the question directly.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivots from the book's thesis (221) to the audience it's meant for.
storyboard.addedInformation: Marks the direct address to the listener — the episode's real point starts here.

storyboard.claim: Recognizing these behavioral loops matters whether you meet them in fiction, friendship, romance, or algorithms.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Skinner box — the mechanism behind the behavioral loops the narration names.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers 222's question: because the same loop appears everywhere.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the pattern (behavioral loops) as the thing worth recognizing, wherever it shows up.

callout.text: THE MECHANICS OF THE SLOT MACHINE

storyboard.claim: Recognizing the slot machine's mechanics is the only way to see your own biology being used against your logic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The slot machine — the human-scale version of the Skinner box just named.
storyboard.onScreenText: THE MECHANICS OF THE SLOT MACHINE
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the abstract 'behavioral loop' (223) its concrete, named form.
storyboard.addedInformation: Connects the clinical mechanism directly to the reader's own experience of being 'weaponized.'

storyboard.claim: Understanding the variable ratio reward and misattributed arousal is the only defense against intermittent reinforcement.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Everyman holding up a shield — understanding as the only protection against the trap.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns 224's warning about the slot machine into what to actually do about it.
storyboard.addedInformation: States that understanding itself — not escape or willpower — is the defense.

storyboard.claim: Understanding this mechanism changes how you evaluate the media you consume and the relationships you tolerate.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Everyman examining their own media and relationships through a magnifier.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the 'defense' in 225 into a concrete habit of scrutiny.
storyboard.addedInformation: Applies the lesson beyond this one book to media and relationships generally.

callout.text: A GIRL TRAPPED WITH A MONSTER

storyboard.claim: Macca didn't just write a girl trapped with a monster — she wrote a book that makes the reader complicit.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery and Gray in silhouette — the asylum story at the center of the book.
storyboard.onScreenText: A GIRL TRAPPED WITH A MONSTER
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the book's plot to set up the reader-complicity point that follows.
storyboard.addedInformation: Restates the premise plainly before the next beat turns it on the reader.

storyboard.claim: Macca's real achievement is making the reader hold the door shut so the story can't get out.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Everyman bracing against a door, holding it shut from the inside.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns 227's trapped girl into the reader's own complicity — the door image now applies to us.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes explicit that the reader, not just Avery, is now holding something shut.

storyboard.claim: Asks the viewer directly: are you enjoying the story, or has the author hacked your nervous system too?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A jolt through the Everyman — the same nervous-system hijack described happening to Avery.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends 228's door image into the direct question closing the episode's argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: Applies Avery's exact mechanism (nervous system hijack) to the viewer, closing the loop.

storyboard.claim: Sign-off: keep questioning what you read, keep looking for the blueprints.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Everyman examining with a magnifier — the habit of scrutiny the episode leaves you with.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closing line, echoing the examination habit built across 222-229.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: a sign-off restating the episode's closing thought rather than adding new content.
